svg.text: Mangrove topographic transect: how to measure the profile
Side view (A, vertical scale exaggerated), one segment (B), plan view (C) and the resulting CSV (D). Not to scale.
A · Side view: stations along the tape, from the low-water mark to the 30 m mark
tape distance from the low-water mark (cumulative)
stations (poles): at every slope change and at most 2 m apart
B · One segment between two stations (dashed box in A)
d = slope distance along the tape
1. Keep the tape taut and straight between the stations.
2. Hold two poles of equal height vertically on the two
3. Sight with the clinometer from the top of the rear pole
to the top of the front pole → inclination α.
4. Read the cumulative tape distance at the front station.
5. Write both on the field sheet; move one station forward.
C · Plan view: straight line, one bearing
D · One row per station → CSV for the notebook
• first row: GNSS fix required (lat, lon, z); inclination empty
• inclination = slope of the segment leading to that station
• lat/lon/z on other rows only for optional RTK ties
• handheld GNSS: z approximate, profile relative to the start
